sections.name: INTRODUCTION
sentences: Ricardo Ellison (hereinafter referred to as “Plaintiff’), claims of Defendants Glen- Gery Corporation and Glen-Gery Corporation, d/b/a Glen-Gery Mid-Atlantic Plant (hereinafter referred to as “Defendants”), a sum in excess of $150,000 in damages upon a cause of action whereof the following is a statement: This action for declaratory, injunctive, monetary, and other appropriate relief is brought by Plaintiff to redress violations by Defendants of rights secured to Plaintiff by the laws of the United States of America.

Zi This action arises under Title VII of the Civil Rights Acts of 1964 (“Title VII”), 42 U.S.C. §2000(e), et seq., as amended by the Civil Rights Act of 1991 at 42 S.C. §1981(a), the Civil Rights Act of 1866, 42 U.S.C. §1981 (“§1981), and the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 1681-1681(x) (“FCRA”), and is brought by Plaintiff to redress arbitrary, improper, unlawful, willful, deliberate and intentional discrimination Case 5:21-cv-04246-EGS Document1 Filed 09/27/21 Page 2 of 8 with respect to his compensation, terms, conditions and privileges of employment by the Defendants, based on his race (African-American).
Plaintiff also asserts a claim under the FCRA for violations of said Act, including being discharged in contravention thereof.

sections.name: STATEMENT OF CLAIMS
sentences: Plaintiff was employed by Defendants from in or about September 8, 2020, until on or about October 14, 2020, when he was terminated from his position of employment as a result of unlawful and discriminatory employment practices complained of herein.
Plaintiff held the position of laborer at the time of his termination.
During his employment, Plaintiff performed his job function in a dutiful and competent manner for Defendants. | At or about the time of his hire, Defendants performed a background check on Plaintiff.
Upon information and belief, Plaintiff was not asked to provide written Case 5:21-cv-04246-EGS Document1 Filed 09/27/21 Page 4 of 8 authorization for his background check.
Approximately three weeks after his hire, on or about October 2, 2020, Plaintiff was informed that he was terminated due to information which appeared on his background check.
Although Plaintiff was not provided a copy of the report, he was told that if he presented information clarifying that the particular entry was dismissed, he could return to work.
Shortly thereafter, Plaintiff provided such information to Defendants, yet was never contacted to return to work.
Thereafter, Plaintiff made several unsuccessful attempts to follow-up with Defendants as to the status of his employment.
Plaintiff went to his place of work on October 14, 2020, and was told, for the first time, that he was instead fired for leaving his line without permission.

Plaintiff disputed this assertion as he was never previously told of any improper conduct on his part. | Moreover, unlike Defendants’ Caucasian personnel, Plaintiff was not issued any disciplinary action for his alleged misconduct and was not afforded any progressive discipline, which would not have resulted in his immediate dismissal for said infraction.
Plaintiff was therefore subjected to differential and disparate standards of treatment on the basis of his race.
The reason asserted by Defendants for Plaintiff's termination was a pretext for racial discrimination.

Plaintiff was also disparately impacted by Defendants’ criminal record Case 5:21-cv-04246-EGS Document1 Filed 09/27/21 Page 5of8 screening practices in that they are neither job-related and nor consistent with business necessity.

Defendants’ actions likewise violated the FCRA for failing to provide Plaintiff with a copy of his background check and a summary of rights, failing to give him an opportunity to review the report and explain any challenged occurrences, failing to provide him with a pre-adverse action notice, and by terminating his employment for pretextual reasons.

sections.name: COUNT I (TITLE VII — Race Discrimination)
sentences: The actions of the Defendants through its agents, servants, and employees, in subjecting the Plaintiff to discrimination in the terms, conditions and privileges of his employment, and in terminating Plaintiffs employment because of his race (African-American), constituted a violation of Title VII of the Civil Rights Acts of 1964 (“Title VII”), 42 U.S.C. §2000(e), et seg., as amended by the Civil Rights Act of 1991 at 42 U.S.C. §1981(a).
The Defendants’ acts of discrimination as aforesaid were intentional, willful and in reckless disregard of Plaintiff's rights and interests.

sentences: The actions of the Defendants, through its agents, servants, and employees, in subjecting the Plaintiff to discrimination in the terms, conditions and privileges of his employment, and in terminating Plaintiff's employment because of her race (African-American), as aforesaid, constituted a violation of §1981.
Defendants’ acts of discrimination as aforesaid were intentional, willful and in reckless disregard of Plaintiff's rights and interests.

sections.name: COUNT III (FCRA)
sentences: The actions of the Defendants, through its agents, servants, and employees, in failing to provide Plaintiff with a copy of the background check and a summary of his rights, failing to give him an opportunity to review the report and explain any occurrences, failing to provide him with a pre-adverse action notice, and by terminating him in a pretextual manner, as aforesaid, constituted a violation of the FCRA.
Defendants’ acts in violation of the FCRA, as aforesaid, were intentional, willful and in reckless disregard of Plaintiffs rights and interests.
